items.prompt: Design a word dictionary with addWord(word) and search(pattern), where '.' in the pattern matches any single letter.
items.why: Matching against many stored words letter by letter, branching at wildcards → a trie with a DFS. A hash set would have to try 26^k expansions of the dots.

items.prompt: Decide whether two strings are anagrams of each other.
items.why: Only exact letter counts matter, no prefixes → a count map (or a 26-slot array).

items.prompt: Given a letter grid and 10,000 dictionary words, return every word that can be traced on the grid through adjacent cells.
items.why: Many words with shared prefixes searched in one space → put them in a trie and run one trie-guided backtracking DFS from each cell.

items.prompt: Given a letter grid and ONE word, decide whether the word can be traced through adjacent cells.
items.why: A single word → plain grid backtracking (mark, recurse, unmark). A trie adds nothing for one word.

items.prompt: Return the maximum value of nums[i] XOR nums[j] over all pairs in an array of 10^5 integers.
items.why: Each number needs its best XOR partner → a binary trie of the bits, walking towards the opposite bit greedily: O(n · bits). A single running XOR (Bitwise XOR pattern) can't pair numbers.

items.prompt: Find the length of the longest substring of s without repeating characters.
items.why: A contiguous substring with a maintainable condition → dynamic sliding window. Tries index word prefixes, not windows.

items.prompt: Replace every word in a sentence by the shortest dictionary root that is a prefix of it.
items.why: "Which stored string is a prefix of this word, shortest first?" → walk the word down a trie of roots and stop at the first end marker.

items.prompt: Count how many distinct strings appear in a list.
items.why: Exact matches only → a hash set. A trie works but is extra machinery when no prefix queries are needed.
